The complex would be built entirely above water.**  Proposed New Sports Stadium - 1958  **A proposal submitted in 1958 for a Pittsburgh stadium built entirely above the Monongahela River.**  **Eventually, the north shore was chosen as the spot for the new "Pittsburgh Stadium." The complex would include hotels, restaurants and a riverfront park to complement the new state-of-the-art multi-purpose stadium.**  **The original prototype was a bit different from the final design. The cost of the stadium was $55 million.**  **In between the ground-breaking and the completion of construction, the structure was given a new name, "Three Rivers Stadium." title: Tidewater Landing Multipurpose Stadium and Mixed-Use Development - LaBella
content: # Tidewater Landing Multipurpose Stadium and Mixed-Use Development. LaBella is providing programming, master planning, and full architectural services for Tidewater Landing, a stadium-anchored, mixed-use development that will be the largest economic development project in the history of Pawtucket, Rhode Island, transforming the city’s waterfront with hundreds of thousands of square feet of new residential and retail development. This mixed-use development also includes **Centreville Bank Stadium**—a 10,500-seat USL Championship League soccer stadium, an indoor events center for amateur sports, a hotel, a food hall, retail shops, parking garages, and a public plaza that serves as a connection between the various buildings and the river. Centreville Bank Stadium is a state-of-the-art, 10,500-seat venue and home to Rhode Island FC of USL Championship soccer. As Rhode Island’s first soccer-specific stadium, it has attracted more sports and entertainment events to Pawtucket. In October 2025, the Centreville Bank Stadium received the 2025 *SportsTravel* Award for Best New or Renovated Venue at the TEAMS Conference & Expo in Columbus, Ohio.
